events.title: WORK presents: Robert Hood, Disco Zombie, Ønyx, & Rubbermiro

artist_notes.name: Robert Hood
artist_notes.note: Detroit minimal-techno originator, M-Plant founder — co-founder of Underground Resistance alongside Jeff Mills and Mad Mike, then reduced the form to its bare drum/bassline essentials on 'Internal Empire' and 'Minimal Nation' (both 1994). Also records as Floorplan (gospel-inflected house). A tracked name.

artist_notes.name: Disco Zombie
artist_notes.note: LA-based techno DJ and producer active in the WORK / Dirty Epic underground orbit — dark, groovy techno sets; hosts the @earlyafters show on KCHUNG Radio.

artist_notes.name: Ønyx
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ active on the city's underground techno circuit; has an RA profile and plays the same WORK/INCOGNITO-adjacent events — limited wider footprint, included on billing confidence.

artist_notes.name: Rubbermiro
artist_notes.note: LA techno DJ (KCHUNG Radio's earlyafters host alongside Disco Zombie) — dark, groovy underground techno; regular on the Dirty Epic / WORK circuit.

enrichment.curator_note: Robert Hood in a TBA warehouse on July 4th is the anti-fireworks plan — stripped, relentless M-Plant minimal with a crew of actual LA heads supporting. WORK's format (address drops day-of) means the room stays self-selecting, which is exactly right for this.
enrichment.description: WORK presents Robert Hood (M-Plant, Detroit) with Disco Zombie, Ønyx and Rubbermiro at a TBA Los Angeles warehouse, 10pm.

verdict.why: Robert Hood is a tracked artist and one of Detroit techno's foundational figures — WORK is a credible underground LA promoter, TBA warehouse on a holiday weekend.

events.title: Midnight Lovers with Eli Escobar (Day & Night)

artist_notes.name: Eli Escobar
artist_notes.note: NYC house/disco lifer since the late '90s (Le Bain, Tiki Disco residencies) — deep New York disco-house knowledge, released on Defected's Classic and his own Night People imprint; remixed Honey Dijon and Lana Del Rey. Reliable, groove-first selector.

enrichment.curator_note: A day-into-night set from a genuine NYC disco-house veteran is a solid Fourth of July anchor if you want the vinyl-groove feeling without chasing a TBA address. Eli Escobar plays it warm and record-collection-deep rather than peak-time.
enrichment.description: Eli Escobar (NYC house/disco DJ) plays a day-and-night set at The Bridge in DTLA, 7pm-2am, $22 presale.

events.organizers: Signal Underground, Canary Sound Werk, Cirra
events.detail: Bay Area dub technicians soundtrack this underground debut. A delight for the senses, this no-phone dance floor invites you to let the music lead you.

artist_notes.name: Day Thief
artist_notes.note: US DJ/producer (Sophie L) working the underground FLINTA*/queer party circuit out of SF/Oakland and NYC — appears on BASEMENT-adjacent bills; leans dark, all-night warehouse techno.

artist_notes.name: Faited
artist_notes.note: Oakland-based DJ (Fait P) from the Envelope Soundsystem/Eris Drew-Octo Octa orbit — underground queer techno and house circuit, more soundsystem-culture than festival-facing.

enrichment.curator_note: Cirra's booked two names straight out of the SF/Oakland queer-underground soundsystem scene (Faited runs sound for Eris Drew's crew) rather than the usual LA warehouse regulars — a genuinely different flavor of afters if you want something rawer than the DTLA circuit.
enrichment.description: Cirra presents a TBA-location DTLA afterhours party with Day Thief, Faited and sosoftly (billed as David Le Brun), 10pm.

verdict.why: Unknown names but TBA DTLA late-night on a Friday from Cirra (a small underground LA party collective) — no red flags, just low-info. Could be good.

events.title: Great Quality Entertainment presents Township Rebellion with Trou and DENYC

artist_notes.name: Township Rebellion
artist_notes.note: Berlin/Cologne techno-house duo (Stil vor Talent, Suara) — shadowy, vocal-accented melodic techno that helped shape the Lane 8/Afterlife-adjacent sound; broke wider after a 2019 Burning Man set connected them to Rufus Du Sol's camp.

artist_notes.name: DENYC
artist_notes.note: LA-based artist (Denise Poole) blending live vocals with dance-heavy basslines — still emerging, limited track record.

enrichment.curator_note: Township Rebellion at 1720 is the real draw — this is the melodic, emotionally-pitched end of techno that runs closer to Lane 8 than to a warehouse hammer, so go in expecting build and atmosphere over pure peak-time. Couldn't turn up anything solid on Trou, so that's an unknown quantity on the bill.
enrichment.description: Great Quality Entertainment presents German melodic-techno duo Township Rebellion with Trou and DENYC at 1720 in the Arts District, 10pm-3am, $21 presale.

verdict.why: Township Rebellion is a South African duo with a genuine afro/deep house following, and 1720 is one of the better warehouse rooms in the Arts District.

artist_notes.name: Mike Servito
artist_notes.note: Detroit-bred, NY-based DJ and longtime Bunker NYC resident — jacking, unpretentious sets that move fluidly through house, acid and techno; a fixture of the queer-underground warehouse circuit for two-plus decades.

artist_notes.name: Jason Kendig
artist_notes.note: Detroit-vet DJ and one-quarter of San Francisco's Honey Soundsystem crew — deep, eclectic house/techno selection; frequent Servito collaborator (Honcho, The Black Madonna's We Still Believe tour).

enrichment.curator_note: SMD pairing Servito and Kendig is a real one — these two have logged years of Honcho and Honey Soundsystem warehouse nights together and know how to build a room slowly rather than just peak-time-blast it. TBA location keeps it self-selecting, which fits the sound.

events.title: Simon Says: Felix Da Housecat
events.venue: The Spotlight (Los Angeles) tech house, electro house, nu-disco

artist_notes.name: Felix Da Housecat
artist_notes.note: Chicago house lifer turned electroclash figurehead — mentored by acid-house originator DJ Pierre in the '80s, ran Radikal Fear Records through the '90s, then broke big with 2001's 'Kittenz and Thee Glitz' (with Miss Kittin), which more or less wrote the electroclash playbook. Deep discography of remixes for Madonna/Britney from that era too.

enrichment.curator_note: A genuine Chicago house/electroclash legend on a small-room bill — this is one of those names where even a random Friday set is worth catching if you're already near The Spotlight.

artist_notes.name: Doc Martin
artist_notes.note: West Coast house pioneer — moved SF to LA in the early '90s, founded the long-running Sublevel label/party (25 years deep in 2026); deep, tribal, acid-inflected house from a genuine scene elder.

artist_notes.name: Lee Burridge
artist_notes.note: UK DJ, founder of All Day I Dream — melodic, organic, Balearic-leaning house; about as close to the European sunset-groove reference point as a festival lineup gets.

artist_notes.name: Justin Martin
artist_notes.note: Dirtybird co-founder — bouncy, quirky, bass-inflected West Coast house ('Sasquatch', 'Buggin''); SF scene royalty.

artist_notes.name: Radio Slave
artist_notes.note: Matt Edwards' techier alias — Rekids co-founder, ex-Ministry of Sound resident; propulsive, muscular house/techno, a genuinely European-pedigreed booking.

artist_notes.name: Mikey Lion
artist_notes.note: Desert Hearts co-founder — psychedelic house/techno out of the SoCal camping-rave scene, warmer and trippier than straight club fare.

artist_notes.name: DJ Colette
artist_notes.note: Chicago house vocalist/DJ (Om Records, Skint) — classic Chicago-lineage vocal house, been in the game since the late '90s.

artist_notes.name: Anton Tumas
artist_notes.note: Subtract Music founder — deep house/techno/hypnotic-electronica selector who ran the beloved 'Subtract On The Pier' Long Beach series; genuinely well-regarded in the SoCal deep-house underground.

artist_notes.name: DAVI
artist_notes.note: Armenian-born, LA-based progressive house producer — early support from Hernan Cattaneo, Nick Warren, John Digweed; polished melodic-prog rather than raw underground.

artist_notes.name: DJ Minx
artist_notes.note: Detroit house matriarch, Women on Wax founder — tracked artist; deep, soulful, dancefloor-first selection.

enrichment.curator_note: This is a real house-music bill, not a generic festival dump — Doc Martin and Lee Burridge alone give it actual lineage, and DJ Minx (already tracked) plus Radio Slave add European/Detroit weight. Long Beach is a haul, but the depth of this lineup earns it.
enrichment.description: Love Long Beach Festival at Shoreline Aquatic Park, 2pm, with a house/tech-house lineup including Doc Martin, Justin Martin, Lee Burridge, Radio Slave, Mikey Lion and DJ Minx.

artist_notes.name: DJ Slugo
artist_notes.note: Chicago ghetto-house/footwork pioneer, founding Dance Mania crew alongside DJ Deeon and Paul Johnson — raw, high-BPM, chant-hook club tracks; the sound Daft Punk sampled on 'Teachers.'

enrichment.curator_note: Baile World is one of LA's best global-club rooms (founded by DJ CQUESTT, built around femme/POC selectors), and landing a Dance Mania originator like DJ Slugo is a real coup — footwork/ghetto-house rather than straight house, so know what you're walking into, but it'll move.
enrichment.description: Secret-location DTLA afterhours party (11pm) from the Baile World series, headlined by Chicago ghetto-house pioneer DJ Slugo.

artist_notes.name: Demuir
artist_notes.note: Toronto-based, Chicago-schooled house producer — Beatport's #1 Jacking House producer 2015/2016, credited with creating the 'Jackin House' genre tag; 600+ tracks deep, releases on Hot Creations and Classic. Funky, sexy, groove-first house.

enrichment.curator_note: Certified Groovers keeps booking real house heads for these TBA nights, and Demuir's jackin'-house pedigree (he basically named the subgenre) makes this a solid groove-forward pick over a lot of the generic 'electronic, TBA' listings this week.
enrichment.description: Certified Groovers presents Demuir at a TBA downtown LA location, 10pm.

artist_notes.name: Chambord
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ/production duo — eclectic, melodic sets pulling in world-music textures alongside more hypnotic electronic passages; a reasonable fit for FLOAT's rooftop-groove daytime format.

enrichment.curator_note: Same FLOAT rooftop-pool formula as the Wisternoff date a week earlier — Chambord's a local, eclectic-melodic booking rather than a marquee name, but the setting alone earns it a look.
enrichment.description: FLOAT rooftop pool party at Level 8 DTLA (2-8pm) with local duo Chambord.

artist_notes.name: Scotty Boy
artist_notes.note: Vegas-based house veteran (25+ years, three Billboard Dance #1s) and founder of DTLA's long-running 'Deep House Brunch' — plays crowd-friendly deep/jackin' house and nu-disco edits, more festival-polish than underground digger.

enrichment.curator_note: Scotty Boy plays it safe and populist — reliable jackin'-house-and-disco-edits energy for a Koreatown late night, but it's closer to brunch-party polish than a proper selector's set.
enrichment.description: Late-night disco/house party (10pm) at Kiss Kiss Bang Bang in Koreatown headlined by house DJ/producer Scotty Boy.

enrichment.curator_note: This is LA's underground Brazilian baile-funk party (Victoria Moura's Club Pivete) — a fun, scrappy corner of the DTLA underground, but it's baile funk/global bass, not house-techno, so treat it as a curiosity rather than a top pick.
enrichment.description: Club Pivete — underground Brazilian baile funk party at a TBA DTLA location, midnight start.

artist_notes.note: Belgian producer (Sam Huybrecht) running his own label/party series Sweet Nothing — a deliberately 'post-genre' set that swings between trance, techno, eurodance and house rather than staying in a lane. Closer to a big-room selector than a groove/disco DJ.

enrichment.curator_note: Late Exchange LA night from a guy who's built a whole identity on not picking a genre — trance-y, eurodance-inflected, more festival-adjacent than a proper house/tech-house selector's set.

events.detail: Open-air fest HARD Summer returns with a globe-trotting line-up boasting Tokischa, salute, Charlotte de Witte, Zack Fox, Shygirl, VTSS and hometown heroes CQUESTT and Dj Warning.

artist_notes.name: Charlotte de Witte
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno powerhouse, KNTXT label boss — hard, hypnotic peak-time techno; a tracked name and one of the strongest bookings on this lineup.

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

artist_notes.name: Maceo Plex
artist_notes.note: Miami-via-Barcelona producer (Eric Estornel) — tech-house and techno crossover, Ellum Audio boss; deep, dark, groove-driven.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish DJ/producer on the harder, rave-leaning end of techno — Bicep's Fabric label, T4T LUV NRG co-founder; a genuinely respected underground name amid the festival billing.

artist_notes.name: Shygirl
artist_notes.note: UK rapper/vocalist and NUXXE co-founder — hyperpop-adjacent club music, Sega Bodega/Arca collaborator; more art-club than DJ set.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Scottish DJ/producer on the UK hard-house/hardcore-revival wave — high-BPM, rave-nostalgic tech house.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

artist_notes.name: Mau P
artist_notes.note: Dutch producer of 'Drugs From Amsterdam' fame — tracked name; big-room tech house with a raw, jacking edge.

artist_notes.name: DJ Seinfeld
artist_notes.note: Swedish-Argentine producer (Armand Jakobsson) who pioneered 'lo-fi house' — tracked name; hazy, nostalgic house that's a shade more tasteful than most of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Chris Lorenzo
artist_notes.note: UK bass/house producer, Half Baked label — tracked name; UK garage-inflected, bass-heavy house.

artist_notes.name: Interplanetary Criminal
artist_notes.note: Manchester producer riding the UK bassline/2-step revival — one of the more interesting names on the bill if you like that skippy, rave-adjacent garage sound.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, RAM Records boss — outside the house/techno lane but a genuine, decades-deep DJ talent if you catch a set.

artist_notes.name: Etari
artist_notes.note: LA-based (Orange County-raised) producer and AUNTIE co-founder — house through trance and techno, with releases on 100% Silk; regular on the Lights Down Low/HARD Summer circuit.

artist_notes.name: Nick León
artist_notes.note: Miami producer on TraTraTrax and Future Times — fuses dembow, reggaeton and dancehall rhythm into house/techno (his own coined term: 'arquitectronica'); one of the more genuinely distinctive club producers right now, sun-bleached and heavy in equal measure.

artist_notes.name: Pegassi
artist_notes.note: Belgian producer (Sam Huybrecht) running his own label/party series Sweet Nothing — a deliberately 'post-genre' set that swings between trance, techno, eurodance and house rather than staying in a lane. Closer to a big-room selector than a groove/disco DJ.

enrichment.curator_note: This is the maximalist, 68-name-deep HARD Summer bill — Charlotte de Witte, VTSS and Amelie Lens give the techno stage real weight, but the day is mostly festival-scale bass/electro/hyperpop stuff outside the lane. Go for a handful of sets, not the whole grounds.
enrichment.description: Day one of HARD Summer at Hollywood Park Grounds, Inglewood — 60+ act electronic/bass festival lineup including Charlotte de Witte, Amelie Lens, VTSS, DJ Snake, Boys Noize and Zedd.

artist_notes.note: Dublin producer (Jack Casey) making atmospheric, vocal-forward melodic house — signed to Lane 8's This Never Happened label; downtempo-leaning and emotive rather than peak-time.

enrichment.curator_note: A rooftop sunset set from a This Never Happened-orbit artist is squarely the golden-hour-groove lane — EMBRZ leans dreamier and more vocal than a straight house DJ, good for the early slot rather than the whole night.
enrichment.description: Sunset rooftop set (5pm) at Harbor House DTLA with Dublin melodic-house producer EMBRZ.

events.title: Midnight Lovers with Isaac Carter, Harrison BDP, Lubelski

artist_notes.name: Isaac Carter
artist_notes.note: London DJ/producer, vocal-led deep house on his own Ochi imprint — championed by Ben UFO, Joy Orbison and Seth Troxler; UK-club lineage (Chicago/Detroit roots filtered through contemporary UK dance).

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Isaac Carter's UK deep-house pedigree (that Ben UFO/Seth Troxler co-sign carries real weight) makes this a stronger TBA-DTLA afterhours than the billing alone suggests — a legit late-night option once Harrison BDP fills in the middle.
enrichment.description: TBA-location DTLA afterhours (starts midnight) with London deep-house producer Isaac Carter, Welsh DJ Harrison BDP, and LA's Lubelski.

artist_notes.name: Phantoms
artist_notes.note: LA duo (Kyle Kaplan, Vinnie Pergola) blurring house and indie-dance — 'alternative electronic,' now on Foreign Family, ODESZA's label. Bigger-room, hooky and radio-adjacent rather than a selector's set.

enrichment.curator_note: This is DTLA pool-party energy from a duo built for festival middle-slots, not the rooftop-groove thing — fine if you want an afternoon out at Level 8, but there's no real DJ-selection angle here.
enrichment.description: Daytime pool party at Level 8 DTLA headlined by LA electronic duo Phantoms, 2pm start.

events.detail: The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.Adapted from S.E. HINTON’s seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA’s iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) and Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, and arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, and direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation."In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self- discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.
